mentions.name: Kodan
mentions.description: A self-solving Kanban tool for mid-sized companies and enterprises with a controllable autonomy level, multiplayer support, a remote coding server, multirepo project support, mobile support, and previews. Its most-used feature is being spun off into a separate standalone product.
mentions.problem: The pain exists, but it's pretty hard to break the integration barrier.
mentions.source_excerpt: I spent ages developing a self-solving Kanban for mid-sized companies and enterprises (https://kodan.dev) - controllable autonomy level, multiplayer support, remote coding server, works on multirepo projects, mobile support, previews, and more.

mentions.name: Kodan
mentions.description: A taskboard that auto-completes easy tasks and specs out and visualizes hard ones. It draws from multiple sources, connects to AI agents via MCP, includes a browser plugin to invite meeting bots to calls, and lets users and testers leave notes on websites that feed into the board. The goal is to make work as simple as dragging tickets around while baking in best practices and review clarity.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I've got a taskboard that auto-completes easy tasks, specs out and visualises hard ones.

Draws from a bunch of sources, MCP-connects to my agents, comes with a browser plugin to invite meeting bots to calls, lets me (and my testers) leave notes on websites which also gets added in.
